notes.3: Over a quarter of candidates thought that the key diagnostic feature for the identification of an insect is the possession of wings rather than the possession of three pairs of legs.
notes.6: A quarter of candidates thought that a palisade cell and a guard cell are both part of the same tissue, possibly indicating a misunderstanding of either the definition of a tissue or of what constitutes an organ.
notes.13: The effect of pH on enzyme action was not well known. The majority of candidates thought incorrectly that the optimum pH for amylase activity is 13.
notes.20: Many candidates did not appreciate that diffusion is a passive process and many did not appreciate that cell division, muscle contraction and protein synthesis all rely on energy released by respiration.
notes.21: More able candidates realised that respiration is an enzyme-controlled reaction whilst many candidates chose one of the options relating to oxygen.
notes.25: Many candidates thought that consumption of alcohol does not cause a loss of muscle coordination.
notes.30: Less able candidates chose one of the options with sunlight, not appreciating that seeds usually germinate in the soil where there is no light.
notes.32: This proved to be the most challenging question on the paper. Almost half of candidates did not realise that a dominant characteristic will be shown in a heterozygous individual.
notes.35: This proved to be the easiest question on the paper, demonstrating the sound grasp that candidates have of food chains.
notes.39: The majority of candidates knew that carbon dioxide contributes to global warming but many candidates chose sulfur dioxide as the other gas rather than methane.
notes.general_comments: No question fell outside the scope of the candidates sitting this paper. The genetics questions were more of a problem to candidates this year than they have been in previous years.
